Design options · presentation only · nothing implemented

Torpedo juice options

task 20261026-003805 v0.17.0 · priority 60 source read at master a894103e3 measurements from 4a650b8f3 (REPORT.html) 2026-11-05

The torpedo already flies well: proportional navigation, a terminal weave, a cold drop and a motor light-off. What it lacks is legibility. Most beats between the press and the end of flight have no cue, and the three ways a flight can end do not read as different events. This page maps every beat, shows where each proposed effect would land, and asks the owner to pick options and a budget.

Does not change
  • Launch, dumb-fire and the no-lock press
  • Fuze, guidance, weave, damage
  • Ammo spend and reload
  • Trajectories, saves, AI, PDC
  • How the launch moves the ship; no launch camera kick
  • HUD, except new stats on the lock readout
May change
  • Particles, lights and meshes on existing events
  • Sounds, including new optional authored sound fields
  • Camera shake inside the existing shake setting

Measured read off a run Source read in code, not run Proposed needs an owner decision Unverified not checked

2 · The measured gap

A dud and a kill end on the same kind of flicker

The earlier research run (arsenal bench, seed 7, Lance bay, target ram_target at 2.62 km) gives a matched pair. Measured The unlocked torpedo touched the target and threw a small orange spark at frame 1730 that was gone by 1736. No sound played and the target kept 2950 / 2950. The locked torpedo fuzed 2.66 units out, played the explosion, and left 275.9 / 2950. At chase-camera range the first frames of both look alike: a small warm point on the target. The player learns the outcome only from a health bar that the unlocked case does not have.

The research did not audition recorded audio. The sound claims come from the per-frame voice log. A shot-down torpedo was not captured on frames. Its cue cells above are marked unverified.

3 · Options

One fix and nine presentation options, grouped by beat

Owner decisions 2026-11-05: every option is approved for implementation. O1 is the light only, with no camera kick. O4 is cut down to extra stats on the lock readout. The HUD tags of O7 and O8 and the pip flash of O9 are dropped. F1 is a defect fix the owner reported, not an optional effect. Each option answers an event that gameplay already raises, or a state it already holds. None adds a rule. Effort is a guess from reading the code (S under a day, M a few days, L a week or more). Cards marked Slice 1 are the recommended first slice.

5 · Recommendation

Ship it in three slices

The measured problem is the ending. Fix the ending first, because a player who cannot tell a kill from a dud from an intercept learns nothing from any earlier cue. Launch heft is the cheapest win and comes second. The flight effects cost the most draw and audio budget, so they come last and only if the first two leave the middle of the flight feeling empty.

Slice 1 · every flight ends with a verdict

F1 wreck fix, O7 Dud cue, O8 Intercept cue, O6a kill stinger

F1 first: a shot-down torpedo must not leave a lit motor behind. Then three endings, three distinct shapes and sounds. Grey and dull for a dud, small and sharp for an intercept, warm and heavy for a kill. Shape and sound both differ, so no ending relies on color alone.

Slice 2 · the press feels like a launch

O1 Launch light, O2 Light-off sound, O9 Rack clunk

A cold light at the tube, a second beat when the motor catches, and a rearm sound. The launch still moves the ship exactly as it does today.

Slice 3 · the flight is readable

O3 Fading trail, O5 Closing tone, O4 time to impact

All approved. Land them last and judge them together in a six-round salvo: the trail costs draw, the tone costs mix space.

6 · Budget and accessibility rules

Rules every chosen option keeps

  • Read the existing GraphicsBudget. Particles gate on particles, shake on shake, lights go through LightFlash and its transient-light cap. Proposed: Low tier keeps the sound half of every option (open below).
  • No new HUD elements (owner decision 2026-11-05). Never carry meaning by color alone: each outcome gets a different shape and sound.
  • No full-screen flash. A six-round salvo fires at 1 per second, under the 3 Hz flash limit, but a blast flash must stay a world light, not a screen overlay.
  • World cues (ignition, dud, intercept, rack) use licensed recorded or library sounds, not generated ones. Only avionics cues (closing tone, kill stinger) may come from scripts/gen-ui-sfx.py. Every imported file records its source and license.
  • Keep the launch, ignition and blast lights in their current ratio. The ignition light is 400 times dimmer than the blast on purpose (render.rs:612-645), so a motor never reads as a warhead.
  • A dud cue must not look or sound like a detonation. No fire colors, no low-frequency boom.
  • Effects observe events; they never feed back into simulation. Matched seeded runs must give identical ammo, health and trajectories with and without the change.
7 · Not proposed

Out of this task

Other HUD juice: torpedo chevrons, edge arrows, outcome tags, pip flashOwner rejected on 2026-11-05. Only the lock readout gains stats.
Launch camera kickOwner rejected on 2026-11-05. The launch must not change how it affects the ship.
Hit-stop or slow motion on a killIt writes the virtual clock, so it changes simulation timing, autopilot deadlines and deterministic replays. It is a gameplay change, not presentation.
Lock-gated player launchEarlier option A. The owner rejected launch changes on 2026-10-31.
Contact warhead for dumb-fireEarlier option B. A new fuze rule; rejected for the same reason.
Screen-space flash or chromatic aberrationAccessibility cost with no information gain over a world light. Hides the HUD at the moment the player reads the result.
Incoming-torpedo warning workThe defense side already has a lock warning (warn_lock.wav) and hostile-torpedo edge arrows (nova_hud/src/edge_indicators.rs:40-86). A separate task if wanted.
Copy-only fixEarlier option D (lesson says "Torpedoes require a combat lock", lessons.rs:730). Still true that the copy is wrong; it is a docs fix, not juice, and can ride with any slice.

Order of work

  • Lane A, gameplay seams: health source, quiet destroys, kill event, trauma floor, throttle keys, trail budget.
  • Lane B, torpedo core (after A): death sorting, kill credit, per-batch reload, time to impact, the new bay fields.
  • Lanes C, D in parallel (after B): torpedo visuals (launch light, flare, trail, shell, dud puff, intercept pop), and every sound.
  • Lane E (after D): content builders, the picked sound files, two generated cockpit sounds, regenerated base content.
  • Lane F last: time to impact on the lock readout. Lane H: docs and changelog.

8 · Proof for a chosen option

How a slice is judged

  • Matched seeded pairs on the arsenal fixture, seed 7: before and after, for launch, flight, dud contact, locked blast and a PDC intercept. Ammo, target health and trajectory traces must match.
  • Capture on an isolated display, never DISPLAY=:0. Inspect frames at High and Low. Listen to the recorded audio, not only the voice log.
  • One six-round salvo per tier: check frame cost against a named reference set, trauma does not saturate, and the lock reticle and target stay readable.
  • A permanent test only for a named stable invariant, for example "a dud contact never plays the detonation sound". No test without owner approval.
Owner decision · 2026-11-05

Approved for implementation

Approved: F1 (all thruster wrecks, ship and torpedo), O1 (light only), O2, O3, O4 (lock readout stats only), O5, O6 (a, b, c), O7, O8, O9. Low tier keeps the sound half of each option. Order: slice 1, then 2, then 3.

Rejected: launch camera kick, torpedo chevrons, edge arrows, outcome tags, pip flash.
